summary: Coeur d'Alene NF lookout near Kellogg, Idaho: 30-foot pole L-4 tower built 1931, destroyed 1968; a visit found two footings and a tie-down; drive-in site.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1968; a visit found two footings and one tie-down still in place

staffing.status: watchers listed from 1934 to 1971 across two sites, which differ on first and last names

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts classes the site as drive-in and reports that the writers drove all the way up; no current road conditions found

events.note: Fred Kottkey, per Idaho Fire Lookouts citing the Wallace Press-Times
Lookout called in because of rain and cool weather, per a Spokane Chronicle item dated September 4, 1936, quoted by Forest Lookouts
Ray Lamareaux, first name on the firelookout.com list
George Howard, per a Kellogg Evening News item cited by Idaho Fire Lookouts; three years after the 1968 destruction date, so the sources conflict

evidence.supports: about five miles southeast of Kellogg, Shoshone County

evidence.quote: This 30' pole L-4 tower, built in 1931, was destroyed in 1968.

evidence.supports: watchers listed from 1938, first name Ray Lamareaux
George Howard listed for 1971, citing a Kellogg Evening News item
September 1936 item: lookout called in because of rain and cool weather
evidence.quote: The lookout on Polaris peak has been called in by forest service officials because of rain and cool weather which has minimized the danger of forest fires.

evidence.supports: visit found two footings and one tie-down; writers drove up
evidence.quote: We were able to drive all the way up to this site and found two remaining footings and one tie-down still in place.

evidence.supports: footings sit downhill from the summit and line up with historic photos of the L-4
evidence.quote: the two we did find are located downhill from the actual summit and line up well with the historic photos of the older L-4 that once stood here.

evidence.supports: rest of the site described as clear
evidence.quote: Other than that, the site is quite clear.

notes_for_editor: Conflict unresolved: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists George Howard in 1971 (citing a Kellogg Evening News item of 06/10/1971, which was not read directly), three years after the 1968 destruction date both sites give. The two sites also differ on the first watchers (1934 and 1935 on Idaho Fire Lookouts; 1938 on firelookout.com). Access: no source states the current access level, so no access key is set; the drive-in note is recorded in visit only. The site is on national forest land, so verify the road and access status before any public guidance. Brief status gone is consistent with all three sources.
